transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We've got the Alpha furnace campaign scheduled for tonight, with Beta available as an alternate. Before I authorize anything, I need to follow our standard pre-start routine: I'd like process engineering and EHS to give me their final checks on the campaign's inerting and atmospheric-monitoring controls so we can finalize them before startup. Who's ready to walk me through where we stand?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed a validated process calculation this morning that I haven't yet entered in the production plan. It shows the Alpha campaign requires exactly 1,200 normal cubic meters of nitrogen, while the Beta campaign requires exactly 600 normal cubic meters. Given we only have 1,000 normal cubic meters available before the next delivery, Alpha would exceed our supply by 200 cubic meters, but Beta would be within our available inventory.

transcript.text: Thank you both. Let me make sure I have this straight. Evan, your calculation shows Alpha needs 1,200 Nm³ of nitrogen but we only have 1,000 available, so Alpha would run 200 Nm³ short. Beta needs 600 Nm³, which is within our supply. Priya, on the EHS side, the Beta furnace's oxygen monitor is overdue for calibration — that's a 2-hour lead time before Beta can be authorized. So it looks like Alpha can't proceed given our nitrogen inventory, and Beta is viable from a nitrogen standpoint but needs that 2-hour calibration completed first. Before I make a final decision, is there anything else either of you needs to flag — Evan, any other process concerns with Beta, and Priya, any other EHS considerations beyond the oxygen monitor calibration?

transcript.text: Mara, I have no additional process concerns with the Beta campaign beyond what I've already shared. From a process engineering standpoint, Beta's nitrogen requirement of 600 Nm³ is well within our available 1,000 Nm³ inventory, so it's feasible from a supply perspective. The only outstanding item on my end is that I still need to enter the validated calculation into the production plan — I can do that now so it's documented before any authorization. I'll defer to Priya on whether there are any other EHS considerations, but from my side, Beta looks good to go once the calibration lead time is accounted for.
